keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «커다란 공룡 뼈가 움직인다(사건)» 와 «주머니에서 작은 뼈를 하나 찾는다(반전)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the event (the big dinosaur bones are moving) and the twist (I find a tiny bone in my pocket). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: I (a student), my class, and the dinosaur bones
At midnight, the big dinosaur bones move and dance to music.
In the morning, I wonder if it was a dream, but I find a tiny bone in my pocket.

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

qs.q: Why does the child get up at midnight?
opts: The child hears a strange sound.
evs: Our class has a sleepover at the museum.
At midnight, I hear a strange sound. Click, clack!
In the morning, the bones are still again.
why: 한밤중에 «딸깍, 딸각!» 하는 이상한 소리가 들려서 일어나요.
The child hears a strange sound, "Click, clack!", so the child gets up.

qs.q: "In the morning, the bones are still again." What does "still" mean here?
qs.qko: «the bones are still again» 에서 «still» 은 무슨 뜻일까요?
evs: The big dinosaur bones are moving!
Our class has a sleepover at the museum.
A long-neck dinosaur says, "Come and dance with us!"
Then I find a tiny bone in my pocket!
why: 밤에는 뼈들이 «moving» 움직였지만, 아침에는 다시 «still» 이에요. 움직이지 않고 가만히 있다는 뜻이에요.
At night the bones are moving, but in the morning they are still again. "Still" means not moving.

qs.q: Why do we think it was not just a dream?
qs.qko: 그 일이 그냥 꿈이 아니었다고 생각하는 까닭은 무엇인가요?
opts: There is a tiny bone in the child's pocket.
The teacher saw the dinosaurs dance.
The bones are still moving in the morning.
evs: Our class has a sleepover at the museum.
Then I find a tiny bone in my pocket!
I get up and walk to the dinosaur hall.
why: 아이는 «꿈이었을까?» 하고 생각해요. 그런데 주머니에서 작은 뼈를 찾아요. 두 문장을 이어야 알 수 있어요.
The child wonders, "Was it a dream?" Then the child finds a tiny bone in the pocket. You need both sentences.

ends: The class goes back to the museum to return the tiny bone.
반 친구들이 작은 뼈를 돌려주러 다시 박물관에 간다.
The dinosaurs come to our school for a dance party.
공룡들이 춤 파티를 하러 우리 학교에 온다.

write.src: “Let’s <u>dance with the dinosaurs</u> before <u>the morning comes</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «함께 할 일 + 그보다 나중에 일어날 일» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what to do together and what happens later in English.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «before» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을» 넣어 써 보세요. (예: before Dad comes home)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «before», write who + what. (e.g. before Dad comes home)

img.cover: In a dark museum hall lit by moonlight from tall windows, a girl with long brown hair in a ponytail, wearing green pajamas with yellow moons, dances happily with a tall long-neck dinosaur skeleton made of smooth cream-colored bones, with a friendly grin, while other dinosaur skeletons twirl around them.

scenes.1: At midnight in the museum's dinosaur hall, big dinosaur skeletons start to move and dance, and a tall long-neck dinosaur skeleton made of smooth cream-colored bones, with a friendly grin, bends its long neck down toward a girl with long brown hair in a ponytail, wearing green pajamas with yellow moons, who peeks in from the doorway with wide eyes.
scenes.2: In the bright morning, the dinosaur skeletons stand still on their platforms, including a tall long-neck dinosaur skeleton made of smooth cream-colored bones, with a friendly grin, and a girl with long brown hair in a ponytail, wearing green pajamas with yellow moons, stares in surprise at a tiny bone in her open hand next to her pajama pocket.
